title: AI Gateways — LiteLLM, Portkey, Kong AI Gateway, Bifrost

questions.question: Which gateway profile has the smallest fixed overhead in the Python comparator?
options: LiteLLM at 10 ms
Portkey at 30 ms
Cloudflare at 2 ms
Kong at 5 ms
questions.explanation: GATEWAY_OVERHEAD assigns Cloudflare 2 ms, less than Kong 5, LiteLLM 10, and Portkey 30.

questions.question: What does AuthService.authenticate return for a presented key whose digest matches no tenant?
options: The first tenant in the map
A new free tenant
A 429 response directly
undefined
questions.explanation: The service walks all known hashes with timingSafeEqual and returns the matching tenant; if none matches, match remains undefined.

questions.question: What state does TokenBucketLimiter maintain per tenant?
options: Tokens, capacity, refill rate, and last timestamp
Only the tenant's model name
A global retry counter shared by all tenants
The full prompt history
questions.explanation: Each Bucket stores tokens, capacity, refillPerSec, and lastNs; allow refills from elapsed time before consuming the request cost.

questions.question: When does callWithRetry stop retrying a provider error?
options: Only after a successful response from another provider
When the error is non-retryable or maxAttempts has been reached
Whenever the first attempt returns 429
After exactly ten attempts regardless of configuration
questions.explanation: The retry loop breaks for a non-retryable error or attempt === cfg.maxAttempts; otherwise it sleeps with exponential backoff and tries again.

questions.question: How does callWithFallback count fallbackHits?
options: It increments once for every provider in the chain
It increments only when all providers fail
It increments when the loop reaches a provider at index greater than zero
It uses the gateway overhead as the count
questions.explanation: The loop executes if i > 0 then fallbackHits++, so reaching the second or later provider counts a fallback attempt.

questions.question: With independent OpenAI and Anthropic error rates of 3% and 2%, what success rate does two-provider fallback approximate?
questions.explanation: Both providers fail with probability 0.03 × 0.02 = 0.0006, so the complement is 0.9994, or 99.94%.
